rationale: Second full pass on the current tree (production diff 868 lines, unit-test diff 1003 lines, live harness) with four lenses: blind, edge-case, acceptance, and tests/harness. Verified against the code: no new production defect that corrupts data in the main scenarios. The remaining issues are (a) the live suite proves less than its evidence table suggests, (b) the parent lookup gives up after 3 passes or when the parent lives in another project dir, and (c) the startup race has no protection once the session status was swept. Deferred: 9 (idle continuation still forwards its own lifecycle hooks, which are its own session's events; lock-free state read fails open; chatty late writer delays OTel; expiry re-runs every tick; inherited uuids stored twice in parse state; summary not back-filled for upgraded states; bash-escape lines count as activity; Ctrl+C close not asserted live; chain A->B->C size). Dismissed: 4 (fractional settle minutes parse correctly; rawLines skipping copies is intended; usage consumed during an idle pass cannot hold own activity by construction; claim that the SessionStart reopen state is not persisted was not reproduced).

findings.title: Live scenarios can pass vacuously or for the wrong reason
findings.problem: S4 stamps the /exit lines with a random sessionId instead of the child's. S8 and S11 only assert 'nothing forwarded after the reopen' with no positive control that the ordinary session reached the backend. S7/S8/S11 never post the native user_prompt record for /exit that QA observed. The fake backend never dedupes, so 'reported once' checks cannot see a double send.
findings.impact: A broken hook-to-daemon wiring would make the reopen scenarios pass; the QA case for 16992 may pass because of a sessionId filter rather than local-command detection.
findings.recommendation: Use the child sessionId in S4; assert 6 usage requests arrived in S8/S11; post native.user_prompt in S7/S8/S11; count raw usage POSTs (not the deduped map) in S5/S10/S12. Re-run the branch and the two baselines and refresh evidence.

findings.title: Committed evidence contains local absolute paths; one unit assertion is a tautology
findings.problem: run.mjs writes the absolute repo path (including the developer's user name) into evidence/*.json. reopen-hold.test.ts asserts that the path returned by its own helper contains the session id. run.mjs also exits 1 for a baseline label other than the exact string 'baseline' and overwrites committed evidence on a partial --only run.
findings.impact: Leaks a local username and layout into the repository; a dead assertion misleads readers; scripted baseline runs break.
findings.recommendation: Write a relative or labelled repo name; replace the tautology with an assertion that nothing was sent; treat labels starting with 'baseline' as expected-to-fail; refuse to overwrite evidence on --only.

findings.title: Parent lookup is final after 3 passes and only searches the child's own directory
findings.problem: ensureInherited stops after MAX_PARENT_LOOKUPS=3 complete lookups (SessionStart, Stop and PreCompact all count), while the parent's continued-in record can land minutes later (D-2 mentions up to 7.5 min). resolveInheritedUuids only reads siblings of the child's transcript. A parent in another project folder yields 'no parent'.
findings.impact: In either case the session is permanently treated as having no parent: the parent's copies are reported and Started is the parent's, which is the original 16992 symptom.
findings.recommendation: Choose: (a) accept and record as D-11, (b) count only lookups made after the session has produced its first own line, or retry on a time basis instead of a pass count, (c) additionally search other project directories (cost and ambiguity risk).

findings.title: Startup-race guard depends on status.endedAt, which is gone after a sweep
findings.problem: For a session not yet marked as reopened the hold applies only when the status file has endedAt and bytes were written after it. After the sweep (the reporter's days-later reopen) there is no status, so a slow resume hook lets the first OTel export go out unheld. Live S11 swept the spool but sent the hook first; S8 raced without sweeping; no scenario combines both.
findings.impact: Claude Code's startup records can move the session end in the reporter's exact situation if the hook is slower than the first export.
findings.recommendation: Choose: (a) accept as part of D-7, or (b) for a session with a saved parse state that has no endedAt in status, hold records written within the settle time of the state file's start, and add a live scenario that sweeps and races.
